     1	/**
     2	 * Replacement for @aztec/bb.js fetchCode browser module.
     3	 *
     4	 * The original uses dynamic import() to load embedded WASM data URIs as a fallback
     5	 * when wasmPath is not provided. Chrome MV3 service workers forbid import() at runtime.
     6	 *
     7	 * This shim replaces the import() fallback with a fetch() to the known WASM asset path.
     8	 * The WASM files are copied to /assets/ by vite-plugin-static-copy from libs/@aztec/bb.js/.
     9	 */
    10	// @ts-expect-error — pako has no types in this context
    11	import pako from "pako"
    12	
    13	const DEFAULT_WASM_PATH = "/assets/barretenberg.wasm.gz"
    14	
    15	export async function fetchCode(multithreaded: boolean, wasmPath?: string): Promise<ArrayBuffer> {
    16		const basePath = wasmPath ?? DEFAULT_WASM_PATH
    17		const suffix = multithreaded ? "-threads" : ""
    18		const filePath = basePath.split("/").slice(0, -1).join("/")
    19		const fileNameWithExtensions = basePath.split("/").pop()!
    20		const [fileName, ...extensions] = fileNameWithExtensions.split(".")
    21		const url = `${filePath}/${fileName}${suffix}.${extensions.join(".")}`
    22	
    23		const res = await fetch(url)
    24		const maybeCompressedData = await res.arrayBuffer()
    25		const buffer = new Uint8Array(maybeCompressedData)
    26	
    27		const isGzip = buffer[0] === 0x1f && buffer[1] === 0x8b && buffer[2] === 0x08
    28		if (isGzip) {
    29			return pako.ungzip(buffer).buffer
    30		}
    31		return buffer.buffer
    32	}

    20	    static async new(wasmPath, logger) {

    35	/**
    36	 * Asynchronous WASM backend that supports both direct WASM and worker-based modes.
    37	 *
    38	 * Worker mode (default): Runs WASM on a worker thread to avoid blocking the main thread. Used in browsers.
    39	 * Direct mode: Runs WASM directly on the calling thread. Used by node.js for better performance.
    40	 */
    41	export class BarretenbergWasmAsyncBackend {
    42	    wasm;

    44	    constructor(wasm, worker) {
    45	        this.wasm = wasm;
    46	        this.worker = worker;
    47	    }
    48	    /**
    49	     * Create and initialize an asynchronous WASM backend.
    50	     * @param options.threads Number of threads (defaults to hardware max, up to 32 for parallel proving)

    52	     * @param options.logger Optional logging function

    56	    static async new(options = {}) {
    57	        // Default to worker mode for browser safety
    58	        const useWorker = options.useWorker ?? true;
    59	        if (useWorker) {

    61	            const worker = await createMainWorker();
    62	            const wasm = getRemoteBarretenbergWasm(worker);

    71	            await wasm.init(module, threads, options.logger, options.memory?.initial, options.memory?.maximum);

     1	import { getSharedMemoryAvailable, getAvailableThreads } from './helpers/browser/index.js';
     2	import { fetchCode } from './fetch_code/index.js';
     3	export async function fetchModuleAndThreads(desiredThreads = 32, wasmPath, logger = () => { }) {
     4	    const shared = getSharedMemoryAvailable();
     5	    const availableThreads = shared ? await getAvailableThreads(logger) : 1;
     6	    // We limit the number of threads to 32 as we do not benefit from greater numbers.
     7	    const limitedThreads = Math.min(desiredThreads, availableThreads, 32);
     8	    logger(`Fetching bb wasm from ${wasmPath ?? 'default location'}`);
     9	    const code = await fetchCode(shared, wasmPath);
    10	    logger(`Compiling bb wasm of ${code.byteLength} bytes`);
    11	    const module = await WebAssembly.compile(code);
    12	    logger('Compilation of bb wasm complete');
    13	    return { module, threads: limitedThreads };
    14	}

     2	// Annoyingly the wasm declares if it's memory is shared or not. So now we need two wasms if we want to be

     4	export async function fetchCode(multithreaded, wasmPath) {
     5	    let url;
     6	    if (wasmPath) {
     7	        const suffix = multithreaded ? '-threads' : '';
     8	        const filePath = wasmPath.split('/').slice(0, -1).join('/');
     9	        const fileNameWithExtensions = wasmPath.split('/').pop();
    10	        const [fileName, ...extensions] = fileNameWithExtensions.split('.');
    11	        url = `${filePath}/${fileName}${suffix}.${extensions.join('.')}`;
    12	    }
    13	    else {
    14	        url = multithreaded
    15	            ? (await import('./barretenberg-threads.js')).default
    16	            : (await import('./barretenberg.js')).default;

**VERIFY**
1. Shim mechanism: verified, with one nuance. The live path starts at [runtime.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/wallet/runtime.ts:91), which calls `BarretenbergSync.initSingleton({ wasmPath: process.env.BB_WASM_PATH })`. In `@aztec/bb.js`, the browser export is selected from [package.json]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/package.json:9), so the extension uses [dest/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/index.js:2), then [barretenberg/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg/index.js:162), then [bb_backends/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/bb_backends/browser/index.js:29), then [bb_backends/wasm.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/bb_backends/wasm.js:20). Of the user-cited `bb_backends/wasm.js` callsites, only line 22 is used by `BarretenbergSync`; lines 63 and 70 are async-only paths. Upstream, [barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:2) imports `./fetch_code/index.js`, which normally re-exports [fetch_code/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/index.js:1). In this app, Vite rewrites that import to [bb-fetch-code.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/shims/bb-fetch-code.ts:15) via [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:87), so the shim is the actual runtime fetch implementation. Nuance: the hook is browser-only in practice because the package root resolves to `dest/browser`, but the `resolveId` predicate itself would also match the node graph’s `./fetch_code/index.js` import from [dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:2).

2. Threads vs singlethreaded: multithreaded is decided by shared-memory availability, not by `desiredThreads`. In [barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:3), `shared = getSharedMemoryAvailable()`, `availableThreads = shared ? navigator.hardwareConcurrency : 1`, `limitedThreads = min(desiredThreads, availableThreads, 32)`, and `fetchCode(shared, wasmPath)` chooses the artifact. [helpers/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/helpers/browser/index.js:2) defines shared-memory availability as `typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' && globalScope.crossOriginIsolated`. So `desiredThreads = 1` does not imply the singlethreaded artifact; it only forces `threads = 1`. If `shared === true`, bb.js still loads `barretenberg-threads...`; if `shared === false`, it loads the singlethreaded payload. Then [barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js:33) creates `WebAssembly.Memory({ shared })`, and only spawns child workers when `threads > 1` at [line 48]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js:48). In your current service-worker path, `BarretenbergSync` always passes `1`, so no child workers are ever created even when the threaded WASM is loaded. Also, the dev-server headers in [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:34) are not the only isolation config; the packaged extension also sets COEP/COOP in [manifest.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/manifest/manifest.config.ts:38). But Chrome’s official extension docs still say service-worker cross-origin isolation is not fully implemented, so you cannot treat the singlethread fallback as impossible: [COEP docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/cross-origin-embedder-policy), [COOP docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/cross-origin-opener-policy?hl=en), [cross-origin isolation docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/cross-origin-isolation?hl=en).

3. What npm `4.2.0` ships: mostly verified, with one packaging nuance. The installed package is `4.2.0` per [package.json]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/package.json:2). It ships a standalone threaded binary at [dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz) and the same under `dest/node-cjs`; there is no standalone singlethreaded `.wasm` or `.wasm.gz` anywhere in the package. The singlethread fallback exists only as a base64-gzipped data URI JS payload in [dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js:1), duplicated into the `dest/node/.../fetch_code/browser/` and `dest/node-cjs/.../fetch_code/browser/` trees. The threaded node `.wasm.gz` is byte-for-byte identical to the browser threaded data-URI payload from [barretenberg-threads.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg-threads.js:1), so swapping that threaded asset in is safe for `4.2.0`.

4. Option evaluation:
- `A` is only safe if you can prove the service worker always has `SharedArrayBuffer` and `crossOriginIsolated === true`. Your code does not prove that, and Chrome’s docs do not guarantee it, so `A` can break the `shared === false` fallback.
- `B` covers both reachable code paths and removes repo vendoring completely. Use the threaded file from `dest/node/.../barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz`, and generate `barretenberg.wasm.gz` from the browser fallback payload in `fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js`.
- `C` is better than today, but it still keeps checked-in binaries around and still needs a source for the singlethread fallback. I also verified your current checked-in [libs]((project root)/packages/extension/libs/@aztec/bb.js) do not match the shipped `4.2.0` bytes, even after gunzip, so drift has already happened.

**RECOMMEND**
Choose `B`.

It is the only option that removes manual vendoring without dropping a real fallback path. Your current runtime is the sync path, so `desiredThreads = 1` means no child workers, but it does not eliminate the singlethreaded artifact path when `shared === false`. Since npm `4.2.0` does not ship a standalone singlethreaded `.wasm.gz`, `B` is the clean way to stay auto-updated on dependency bumps and still cover both branches.

Implementation detail: do not gunzip+regzip the browser fallback. The file in [barretenberg.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js:1) already contains gzip bytes; just base64-decode and emit them as `barretenberg.wasm.gz`. Use the existing `resolvePackageFile()` helper in [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:8) so Bun’s package layout does not matter. Keep `BB_WASM_PATH` at `/assets/barretenberg.wasm.gz` as defined in [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:211); the shim appends `-threads` itself.

Main risks with `B`: it depends on bb.js’s internal file layout and the data-URI format staying stable. Make the build fail loud if the source files move, if the data URI prefix changes, or if the threaded browser payload no longer hashes identically to `dest/node/.../barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz`.

**GAPS-IN-MY-READ**
1. The `resolveId` hook is broader than its comment. Today it is safe because the browser export wins, but if a node bb.js graph were ever bundled, the hook would rewrite that too. Tightening the predicate to browser-only paths would make the intent match the implementation. See [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:81).

2. The shim does not check `res.ok`. A missing asset will fail later as a gzip or `WebAssembly.compile` error instead of a clear 404. See [bb-fetch-code.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/shims/bb-fetch-code.ts:23).

3. The shim should not special-case `desiredThreads = 1`; the right split is still `shared` vs non-`shared`. What it does need is the correct filenames. If someone points `BB_WASM_PATH` at `barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz`, the shim will synthesize `barretenberg-threads-threads.wasm.gz`. See [bb-fetch-code.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/shims/bb-fetch-code.ts:16).

4. If upstream ever makes the threaded browser payload differ from `dest/node/barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz`, swapping stops being safe. The likely failures are `WebAssembly` validation/link errors for shared-memory expectations or JS/WASM ABI drift. For `4.2.0`, they are exactly identical.

**VERIFY**
1. Shim mechanism: verified, with one nuance. The live path starts at [runtime.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/wallet/runtime.ts:91), which calls `BarretenbergSync.initSingleton({ wasmPath: process.env.BB_WASM_PATH })`. In `@aztec/bb.js`, the browser export is selected from [package.json]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/package.json:9), so the extension uses [dest/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/index.js:2), then [barretenberg/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg/index.js:162), then [bb_backends/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/bb_backends/browser/index.js:29), then [bb_backends/wasm.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/bb_backends/wasm.js:20). Of the user-cited `bb_backends/wasm.js` callsites, only line 22 is used by `BarretenbergSync`; lines 63 and 70 are async-only paths. Upstream, [barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:2) imports `./fetch_code/index.js`, which normally re-exports [fetch_code/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/index.js:1). In this app, Vite rewrites that import to [bb-fetch-code.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/src/shims/bb-fetch-code.ts:15) via [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:87), so the shim is the actual runtime fetch implementation. Nuance: the hook is browser-only in practice because the package root resolves to `dest/browser`, but the `resolveId` predicate itself would also match the node graph’s `./fetch_code/index.js` import from [dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:2).

2. Threads vs singlethreaded: multithreaded is decided by shared-memory availability, not by `desiredThreads`. In [barretenberg_wasm/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/index.js:3), `shared = getSharedMemoryAvailable()`, `availableThreads = shared ? navigator.hardwareConcurrency : 1`, `limitedThreads = min(desiredThreads, availableThreads, 32)`, and `fetchCode(shared, wasmPath)` chooses the artifact. [helpers/browser/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/helpers/browser/index.js:2) defines shared-memory availability as `typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' && globalScope.crossOriginIsolated`. So `desiredThreads = 1` does not imply the singlethreaded artifact; it only forces `threads = 1`. If `shared === true`, bb.js still loads `barretenberg-threads...`; if `shared === false`, it loads the singlethreaded payload. Then [barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js:33) creates `WebAssembly.Memory({ shared })`, and only spawns child workers when `threads > 1` at [line 48]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg_wasm_main/index.js:48). In your current service-worker path, `BarretenbergSync` always passes `1`, so no child workers are ever created even when the threaded WASM is loaded. Also, the dev-server headers in [vite.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/vite.config.ts:34) are not the only isolation config; the packaged extension also sets COEP/COOP in [manifest.config.ts]((project root)/packages/extension/manifest/manifest.config.ts:38). But Chrome’s official extension docs still say service-worker cross-origin isolation is not fully implemented, so you cannot treat the singlethread fallback as impossible: [COEP docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/cross-origin-embedder-policy), [COOP docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/cross-origin-opener-policy?hl=en), [cross-origin isolation docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/cross-origin-isolation?hl=en).

3. What npm `4.2.0` ships: mostly verified, with one packaging nuance. The installed package is `4.2.0` per [package.json]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/package.json:2). It ships a standalone threaded binary at [dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/node/barretenberg_wasm/barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz) and the same under `dest/node-cjs`; there is no standalone singlethreaded `.wasm` or `.wasm.gz` anywhere in the package. The singlethread fallback exists only as a base64-gzipped data URI JS payload in [dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js:1), duplicated into the `dest/node/.../fetch_code/browser/` and `dest/node-cjs/.../fetch_code/browser/` trees. The threaded node `.wasm.gz` is byte-for-byte identical to the browser threaded data-URI payload from [barretenberg-threads.js]((project root)/packages/extension/node_modules/@aztec/bb.js/dest/browser/barretenberg_wasm/fetch_code/browser/barretenberg-threads.js:1), so swapping that threaded asset in is safe for `4.2.0`.

4. Option evaluation:
- `A` is only safe if you can prove the service worker always has `SharedArrayBuffer` and `crossOriginIsolated === true`. Your code does not prove that, and Chrome’s docs do not guarantee it, so `A` can break the `shared === false` fallback.
- `B` covers both reachable code paths and removes repo vendoring completely. Use the threaded file from `dest/node/.../barretenberg-threads.wasm.gz`, and generate `barretenberg.wasm.gz` from the browser fallback payload in `fetch_code/browser/barretenberg.js`.
- `C` is better than today, but it still keeps checked-in binaries around and still needs a source for the singlethread fallback. I also verified your current checked-in [libs]((project root)/packages/extension/libs/@aztec/bb.js) do not match the shipped `4.2.0` bytes, even after gunzip, so drift has already happened.

**RECOMMEND**
Choose `B`.

It is the only option that removes manual vendoring without dropping a real fallback path. Your current runtime is the sync path, so `desiredThreads = 1` means no child workers, but it does not eliminate the singlethreaded artifact path when `shared === false`.
